paper_sections.title: Effective amygdala-prefrontal connectivity predicts individual differences in successful emotion regulation
Prefrontal network underlying the down-regulation of emotion
Amygdala-prefrontal network underlying the up-regulation of emotion

description.value: The study examined whether individual differences in successful cognitive reappraisal of aversive pictures are associated with task-dependent effective connectivity between the left inferior frontal gyrus or left amygdala and other emotion-regulation regions.

design.value: Twenty-three right-handed subjects performed an event-related fMRI emotion-regulation task in which they used cognitive reappraisal to increase or decrease their emotional responses, or passively looked at negative or neutral pictures. Reappraisal success scores were entered as predictors of psychophysiological interaction maps.

description.value: After each emotion regulation phase subjects rated their current emotional state on a scale from 1 (not negative) to 4 (very negative).
Skin-conductance data were decomposed into continuous tonic and phasic activity; SCRs were defined as a deflection of at least 0.01 µS occurring 1–8 s after stimulus onset.

Twenty-three right-handed subjects (mean age = 25.70 years, s.d. = 5.95 years; 12 female) participated in the study. Subjects had normal or corrected to normal vision, gave written, informed consent to participate in the study and had no history of neurological or psychiatric disease.

inclusion_criteria.value: normal or corrected to normal vision

exclusion_criteria.value: no history of neurological or psychiatric disease

medical_condition.value: no history of neurological or psychiatric disease

diagnostic_instrument.value: general health questionnaire and fMRI safety screening form

task_description.value: Subjects were presented with highly arousing and aversive pictures while using cognitive reappraisal to increase, maintain, or decrease their emotional responses.

instructions.value: In the ‘Increase’ condition, subjects were asked to engage themselves with the depicted situation and to increase their sense of subjective closeness. In the ‘Decrease’ condition subjects were instructed to reduce the intensity of the negative emotion by distancing themselves from the image by becoming a detached observer. In the ‘Look’ condition, subjects were asked to view the neutral or negative stimuli attentively and allow themselves to experience any emotional responses without trying to manipulate them.

stimuli.value: 126 aversive and 42 neutral pictures from the International Affective Picture System (IAPS).

task_performance_measures.value: current emotional state ratings on a four-point Likert scale from 1 to 4

instrument.value: 3.0 T Magnetom TrioTim MRI scanner (Siemens, Erlangen, Germany) with a 12-channel head coil

description.value: Functional images were acquired using a T2*-weighted, gradient-echo planar imaging pulse sequence recording 37 sections oriented parallel to the anterior and posterior commissure.

number_of_volumes.value: 285 whole brain volumes per experimental run

instrument.value: 3.0 T Magnetom TrioTim MRI scanner (Siemens, Erlangen, Germany) with a 12-channel head coil

description.value: A high-resolution 3D T1-weighted dataset was acquired for each subject.

instrument.value: BrainAmp GSR-module, Brain Products, Gliching, Germany

description.value: EDA was recorded using two cup electrodes with an internal impedance of 15 kΩ (7 mm) filled with isotonic paste and attached to the proximal phalanges of the index and middle fingers on the left hand, using constant voltage electrode excitation.

reason_no_modality_class_used.value: The recording is a physiological measure rather than MRI, EEG, fNIRS, or PET.

description.value: Pre-processing of fMRI data included 3D-motion-correction, temporal high pass filtering, linear trend removal, slice scan time correction, spatial smoothing, and transformation into Talairach space.

steps.value: spatial smoothing (Gaussian smoothing kernel, 8 mm full width half maximum)

model_settings.value: Separate regressors were specified for the instruction cue, rating, and the four task conditions. PPI interaction terms were entered into voxelwise regressions with the seed time series, the original GLM regressors, and reappraisal success scores as a covariate.

software.value: BrainVoyager QX 2.3.1 (Brain Innovation, Maastricht, The Netherlands)

description.value: Subjects were asked to engage themselves with the depicted situation and to increase their sense of subjective closeness to the displayed events.

condition_kind.value: reappraisal task state for up-regulation of emotion

description.value: Subjects were instructed to reduce the intensity of the negative emotion by distancing themselves from the image by becoming a detached observer.

condition_kind.value: reappraisal task state for down-regulation of emotion

description.value: Subjects were asked to view negative stimuli attentively and allow themselves to experience or feel any emotional responses without trying to manipulate them.
Subjects were asked to view neutral stimuli attentively and allow themselves to experience or feel any emotional responses without trying to manipulate them.

multiple_comparison_method.value: family wise error (FWE) thresholds using the alphasim procedure

interpretations.value: Reappraisal was associated with increased responses in prefrontal regions including superior frontal, medial frontal, middle frontal and inferior frontal gyri as well as superior temporal gyrus.

multiple_comparison_method.value: FWE cluster level correction using AlphaSim

interpretations.value: The contrast revealed increased activity in left IFG, SFG, and STG.

multiple_comparison_method.value: FWE cluster level correction using AlphaSim

interpretations.value: The contrast revealed enhanced responses in left MFG, SFG, IFG, STG and pre-central gyrus.

name.value: Univariate ROI analyses of bilateral amygdala

spatial_scope.value: one or more regions of interest

roi_definition.value: anatomically defined using the Anatomy Toolbox

definition.value: Differential activity between Increase and Decrease, Decrease and Look-Negative/Look-Neutral, or Increase and Look-Negative/Look-Neutral

interpretations.value: This analysis was conducted to provide evidence of activity related to emotion regulation and to support the applicability of the following PPI analysis.

name.value: Task-related PPI analysis with success scores as covariate for left IFG seed region: positive correlation during up-regulation

definition.value: Increase success predicted a positive correlation with effective coupling of the left IFG seed and left STG, VMPFC and bilateral amygdalae during Increase > Look-Negative

multiple_comparison_method.value: FWE cluster level correction using AlphaSim

target_regions.value: left STG, VMPFC and bilateral amygdalae

interpretations.value: During the up-regulation of emotion, better Increase success was associated with stronger effective coupling between the left IFG and left STG, VMPFC and bilateral amygdalae.

name.value: Task-related PPI analysis with success scores as covariate for left IFG seed region: negative correlation during up-regulation

definition.value: Increase success negatively correlated with effective coupling of the left IFG seed and pgACC, DMPFC, caudate, right insula, left IPL, right MFG, right STG and right IFG during Increase > Look-Negative

multiple_comparison_method.value: FWE cluster level correction using AlphaSim

target_regions.value: pgACC, DMPFC, caudate, right insula, left IPL, right MFG, right STG and right IFG

interpretations.value: A negative correlation was observed between Increase success and connectivity of left IFG with DMPFC and pgACC during up-regulation.

name.value: Task-related PPI analysis with success scores as covariate for left IFG seed region: positive correlation during down-regulation

definition.value: Decrease success positively correlated with effective coupling of the left IFG seed and DLPFC, DMPFC, right MTG and STG during Decrease > Look-Negative

multiple_comparison_method.value: FWE cluster level correction using AlphaSim

target_regions.value: DLPFC, DMPFC, right MTG and STG

interpretations.value: Down-regulation of emotion was associated with increased effective connectivity in a prefrontal network, including the left VLPFC, DLPFC and DMPFC, depending on reappraisal success.

name.value: Task-related PPI analysis with success scores as covariate for left IFG seed region: negative correlation during down-regulation

definition.value: Decrease success negatively correlated with effective coupling of the left IFG seed and right IFG, left SFG/VMPFC and left orbital gyrus during Decrease > Look-Negative

multiple_comparison_method.value: FWE cluster level correction using AlphaSim

target_regions.value: right IFG, left SFG/VMPFC and left orbital gyrus

interpretations.value: Decreased coupling between left IFG and VMPFC during down-regulation was correlated with greater reappraisal success.

name.value: Task-related PPI analysis with success scores as covariate for left amygdala seed region: positive correlation during up-regulation

roi_definition.value: anatomically defined using the Anatomy Toolbox

definition.value: Increase success positively correlated with coupling between the left amygdala seed and left IFG, left MFG, left SFG, sgACC, left STG, left insula, left IPL, left MTG and left parahippocampal gyrus during Increase > Look-Negative

multiple_comparison_method.value: FWE cluster level correction using AlphaSim

target_regions.value: left IFG, left MFG, left SFG, sgACC, left STG, left insula, left IPL, left MTG and left parahippocampal gyrus

interpretations.value: Increased effective coupling between the IFG with the amygdala correlated positively with reappraisal success for the Increase condition.

name.value: Task-related PPI analysis with success scores as covariate for left amygdala seed region: negative correlation during up-regulation

roi_definition.value: anatomically defined using the Anatomy Toolbox

definition.value: Increase success negatively correlated with effective connectivity between the left amygdala seed and right SFG/OFC during Increase > Look-Negative

multiple_comparison_method.value: FWE cluster level correction using AlphaSim

interpretations.value: Effective connectivity between the left amygdala and right SFG/OFC was negatively correlated with Increase success.

roi_definition.value: anatomically defined using the Anatomy Toolbox

definition.value: Left amygdala activity was positively correlated with activity in bilateral fusiform gyri, right parahippocampal gyrus and occipital cortex and Decrease success during down-regulation

multiple_comparison_method.value: FWE cluster level correction using AlphaSim

target_regions.value: bilateral fusiform gyri, right parahippocampal gyrus and occipital cortex

interpretations.value: Activity in the left amygdala was positively correlated with activity in visual and parahippocampal regions and Decrease success.
